stem.text: A car moves along a straight road with positive velocity v(t) meters per second, where v is differentiable and t is measured in seconds. Measured values are v(0) = 10, v(3) = 14, v(6) = 20, v(9) = 18. Find the approximation to \( \int_{0}^{9} v(t)\,dt \), the distance, in meters, that the car travels from t = 0 to t = 9, given by a trapezoidal sum with the three subintervals indicated by these values. Give the exact value.

worked_solution.text: Each subinterval contributes its width times the average of its two endpoint values: \( 3 \cdot \frac{10 + 14}{2} = 36 \); \( 3 \cdot \frac{14 + 20}{2} = 51 \); \( 3 \cdot \frac{20 + 18}{2} = 57 \).

distractor_derivations.A: left Riemann sum used in place of the trapezoidal sum
distractor_derivations.C: trapezoid area taken as width times the sum of the two endpoint values, with no division by 2
distractor_derivations.D: factor 1/2 applied to the last trapezoid only
